findings.title: Segment key type changed from SET to ZSET without migration, so in-flight keys break on deploy
findings.body: The per-segment key type changes from a Redis SET to a sorted set: sadd becomes zadd here, sscan becomes zscan in _load_segment_data, and sunionstore becomes zunionstore in add-buffer.lua. The key names (span-buf:s:{...}) are unchanged and segment keys live for up to redis_ttl (3600s). During a rolling deploy, or for up to an hour after, old-version SET keys still exist. New code then hits WRONGTYPE on zadd, on zcard/zunionstore/zpopmin inside the Lua script, and on zscan in the flusher. redis-py pipelines raise on command errors, so process_spans fails for any batch touching a legacy key, and flush_segments can fail for every segment in the same batch. That stalls ingestion and flushing until the old keys expire. The fix needs a new key prefix or explicit handling of the type mismatch.

findings.title: zunionstore uses default SUM aggregation, corrupting scores of members present in both sets
findings.body: ZUNIONSTORE without an AGGREGATE option sums scores. When a member (same payload) already exists in set_key and is also in the source key, for example a redelivered span, its score becomes the sum of two end timestamps (about 3.4e9) instead of end_timestamp_precise. zpopmin uses these scores to choose which spans to evict, so eviction order is corrupted. The same problem applies at line 53 for the parent key. Use AGGREGATE MAX or MIN so scores remain timestamps.

findings.title: Span eviction at 1000 is silent: no metric or log, and it replaces an observable limit
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin silently deletes the lowest-scored (earliest-ending) entries. The buffer.py change also removes the old flush-time guard, which logged an error and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded. Segments that used to be dropped and logged are now silently truncated, and operators have no signal that spans are being discarded. Add a counter or log for the number of evicted spans.

findings.title: Redirect-chain walk bound lowered from 10000 to 1000 without explanation
findings.body: The loop bound changed from 10000 to 1000 and the comment that documented the limit was deleted. The change is unrelated to span eviction and is not mentioned in the PR. Redirect chains deeper than 1000 now stop early, leaving set_span_id at an intermediate span, so later spans are attached to the wrong segment with no error or metric. Restore the original bound or justify the change explicitly.

findings.title: Forward-cursor offset clamp changes BasePaginator behavior for all paginated endpoints
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result is shared by DateTimePaginator and Paginator, which many endpoints use. The new line clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors. Previously a negative offset made queryset slicing raise. Now it silently returns the first page. The same negative offset on a prev cursor still passes through unchanged and still raises, so the behavior is inconsistent. The comment on lines 179-181 says negative offsets are 'allowed' for bidirectional paging, but forward pages now do the opposite. No tests cover this change, and it is not gated behind the new optimized path.

findings.title: Negative cursor offset is passed to queryset slicing, which Django rejects with a 500
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset is negative, start_offset is passed unchanged to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet does not support negative indexing and raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'). An admin who sends optimized_pagination=true with a negative cursor offset gets an unhandled 500. The comments at lines 874-880 claim the ORM 'handles negative slicing automatically' and that this exposes data 'beyond normal pagination bounds'; neither is true. The class also copies BasePaginator.get_result (line 821 onward) almost line for line, so the two implementations will drift.

findings.title: organization_context.member is dereferenced without a None check
findings.body: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is Optional. For a non-superuser, the expression organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError if there is no membership record. Whether this is reachable depends on OrganizationAuditPermission admitting non-members, which this diff does not show. Guard with a None check, or confirm the permission guarantees membership.

findings.title: New optimized_pagination branch and its admin gating have no tests
findings.body: The branch that switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True, the superuser/global-access gate, and the fallback to DateTimePaginator are all untested. The negative-offset path that 500s for admins (paginator.py line 882) would be caught by even a single endpoint test. Add tests for the admin path, the non-admin fallback, and a negative cursor.

findings.title: Comment claims a capability that this change does not implement
findings.body: The added comment says it is a 'performance optimization' that allows negative offsets for 'efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions'. The only change is this comment: int(offset) was already unvalidated. Downstream, forward pages clamp negatives to 0 and prev pages pass them into queryset slicing, which raises. The comment advertises behavior that does not exist and will mislead future readers.

findings.title: Module docstring still describes span-buf:s:* keys as sets
findings.body: The glossary says span-buf:s:* keys are 'the actual set keys', and the flow above says payloads are added to 'the set'. After this change these keys are sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise, which is what the eviction and flush logic depends on. The docs should say so.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now a dead parameter; the eviction limit is hard-coded to 1000 in Lua
findings.body: SpansBuffer still accepts max_segment_spans (default 1001), but nothing reads it. Its only use, the span-count check in _load_segment_data, was removed. The real limit is the hard-coded 1000 in add-buffer.lua line 62. Callers tuning this parameter get no effect, and the two limits disagree. Either pass the limit to the script through ARGV or remove the parameter.

findings.title: Tests do not cover eviction, score ordering, or the set-to-zset change
findings.body: The PR's purpose is eviction above 1000 spans, but no test inserts more than 1000 spans or checks which spans survive. Every fixture uses the same constant end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0, so score-based ordering is never exercised. The zunionstore SUM collision is also untested, as is the old-SET-key compatibility problem. Add a test that inserts more than 1000 spans with distinct end timestamps and checks that the latest 1000 survive, plus a case where the same payload arrives twice.

findings.title: Unrelated audit-log, paginator, and cursor changes are bundled into a spans-buffer PR with a placeholder description
findings.body: The PR title describes a spans buffer optimization, and the description is only 'Test 2'. The diff also changes the audit-log endpoint, adds an experimental pagination class to api/paginator.py, and changes utils/cursors.py. Nothing in the description explains why these belong together or how they are meant to behave. Split them into separate PRs with descriptions, or document the intent.
